title: Flexural Rigidity Measurements of Biopolymers Using Gliding Assays
protocol: Prepare ahead of gliding assay by polymerizing 0.5 mg microtubules sparsely labeled with a bright organic fluorophore.
Store the prepared microtubules at room temperature, light protected with aluminum foil for up to two weeks.
Purify biotin-kinesin21 at approximately 1 μM and store in -80 °C in 5 μl aliquots for individual experiments.
Prepare assay buffer (AB) of 50 mM imidiazole, 50 mM potassium chloride (KCl), 4 mM magnesium chloride (MgCl2), 2 mM ethylene glycol tetraacetic acid (EGTA), pH 6.7.
Sterile filter the prepared assay buffer and store at 4 °C.
Dissolve biotinylated bovine serum albumin (biotin-BSA) to 2 mg/ml in AB.
Filter the dissolved biotin-BSA with a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Store the filtered biotin-BSA at -80 °C in 100 μl aliquots for long periods, or at 4 °C for up to one month.
Dissolve streptavidin (SA) to 10 mg/ml in AB.
Filter the dissolved SA with a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Store the filtered SA at -80 °C in 20 μl aliquots for long periods, or at 4 °C for up to two weeks.
Dissolve α-casein to 5 mg/ml in AB.
Filter the dissolved α-casein with a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Store the filtered α-casein at -80 °C in 100 μl aliquots for long periods, or at 4 °C for up to two weeks.
Dissolve dithiothreitol (DTT) in deionized water at 200 mM and store at -20 °C in 100 μl aliquots.
Thaw the DTT only as needed and use within 8 hr of thawing.
Dissolve paclitaxel in HPLC-grade dimethyl sulfoxide at 4 mM.
Store paclitaxel solution in 10 μl aliquots at -80 °C for long-term storage, or at -20 °C for short-term use.
Use paclitaxel within 8 hours of thawing; can be refrozen.
Dissolve glucose in deionized water at 120 mg/ml.
Store glucose solution in 100 μl aliquots at -20 °C.
Can be refrozen.
Dissolve adenosine triphosphate in deionized water at 150 mM, pH 7.0.
Store ATP solution in 5 μl aliquots at -80 °C for long-term storage.
Use within 8 hours of thawing.
Prepare oxygen scavenging stock by dissolving glucose oxidase and catalase into total assay buffer.
Centrifuge briefly to pellet solids; filter supernatant with a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Store at -80 °C in 10 μl aliquots for long-term storage, or at 4 °C for up to one week.
Prepare AB by mixing 1 ml of assay buffer with 10 μl DTT stock (AB with 2 mM DTT).
Keep AB at room temperature.
Prepare bio-BSA buffer by mixing 40 μl biotin-BSA stock with 40 μl AB.
Keep bio-BSA buffer at room temperature.
Prepare BSA buffer by mixing 645 μl AB with 5.5 μl BSA (1 mg/ml).
Keep BSA buffer at room temperature.
Prepare SA buffer by mixing 57 μl AB with 3 μl streptavidin stock (0.5 mg/ml).
Keep SA buffer at room temperature.
Mix 200 μl of BSA buffer, 50 μl casein stock, and 0.8 μl of 15 μM ATP to prepare α-casein buffer.
Mix 95 μl α-casein buffer, 2.5 μl glucose stock, 1 μl 100x oxygen scavenging mix, 1 μl paclitaxel stock, and 1 μl 2-mercaptoethanol under a fume hood to prepare fluorescence anti-bleach buffer.
Construct four flow lanes between two coverslips using vacuum grease as a spacer.
Wash 10 μl of bio-BSA buffer into each lane.
Incubate the lanes for 5 minutes.
Wash each lane three times with 15 μl BSA buffer to remove free biotin-BSA.
Wait up to 2 hours after washing SA-buffer into each lane.
Wash each lane three times with 15 μl BSA buffer.
Wash each lane with 15 μl α-casein buffer.
Dilute kinesin to 10 nM in α-casein buffer.
Wash each lane with 15 μl of the kinesin-α-casein solution.
Wait 15 min for biotinylated kinesin to bind specifically to surface-bound streptavidin.
Dilute paclitaxel to 40 μM in room-temperature α-casein buffer.
Wash each lane with 15 μl of the paclitaxel solution.
Dilute fluorescently labeled microtubules 1:100-1:1,000 in fluorescence anti-bleach buffer with 1 mM ATP.
Wash 15 μl into one lane and observe within 30 min using fluorescence microscopy.
Set illumination intensity so that single fluorophores do not photobleach more quickly than 100 seconds.
Use laser excitation at a power setting of approximately 3-5 mW.
Collect sequences of images for analysis, aiming for 600 images at 5 Hz (2 minutes total).
Ensure sequences are long enough for microtubules to traverse the entire field-of-view.
Calculate the tangent angle at each point along the trajectory.
Calculate <cosθs> by averaging the cosine of the angle difference for every pair of points separated by a path-length s.
Fit <cosθs> to Eq. 1 to find the persistence length for a single microtubule or group of microtubules.
Weight individual data points in the fit by the number of independent values of cosθs used to compute the average.
